Prop Edge Engine · NFL 2026 · Week 3

Week 3 Picks

Paper picks, logged before kickoff and scored Monday. The model has not yet shown it can beat the book in Week 1, so every pick here is an argument, not a promise. This is analysis, not advice.

Built Sun Oct 4, 9:58 am PDT from DraftKings odds captured 2026-09-27 at 09:13 ET. Next update: Friday Sep 11 evening, after the 4 pm ET injury report (Week 1 practice reports start Wed Sep 9). How the picks are made.

How to read this page
Paper picks. Two weeks in, the engine's numbers have been further from the results than the book's (0.155 against 0.142, then 0.150 against 0.145), its favorable calls have hit at the book's rate, and the misses are players whose roles changed since last season, which the engine will not see until a player has four games. The three role fixes are not built yet. This week the sheet keeps the engine's rule, requires two weeks of usage that fit the rung for a Play (last week's one-week check did not help and is not repeated as a filter), and drops only players who are out, whose quarterback changed, or who have not played. Logged before kickoff, scored Tuesday.

Three views. Picks is the sheet: the legs worth a bet, each with its price, the chance the price implies and the chance the model gives it. Games has one card per game in DraftKings order: kickoff, venue, roof, total, spread, the kickoff forecast, the verdict, the pick and its checks, the book's main lines and the players the model covers. All odds is every ladder the book listed, every rung, beside the model's chance.

Verdicts. Play means we would bet it: our number says it hits more often than the price suggests, the player did it often enough last year to back that up, and the defense he faces does not argue against it. A Play also has to keep at least 10 points of edge in the worst case, meaning if the opposing defense repeats last season in full (the Sensitivity line on each pick). Lean means we like it but something real gets in the way, so we are not betting it and it stays out of parlays; if you bet it anyway, bet small. Pass means the price is fair or too short, so there is no bet.

Parlays. Legs in different games multiply exactly, so the slip price is the product of the leg prices. For legs in the same game DraftKings reprices for correlation, and the displayed price will be lower than the product shown.

Weather. Each card shows the roof and the kickoff-hour forecast: weather.gov when its hourly forecast reaches the kickoff (about 6.5 days out), Open-Meteo before that, each labelled with the source. Rain enters the model as a chance shared by everyone in the game; wind of 15 mph or more shortens the passing game; indoor games carry no weather term.

Players tables. QB is the passer expected to start ("new" marks a change from last season, which the model discounts). Role is the share of the team's pass plays the receiver ran a route on last season, plus expected carries for backs; it is the volume input the model uses. Snap percent is for reference.

On every priced rung the book was closer than the model for the third week (0.143 against 0.139), and in 10 of 15 games. The model was closer only on receptions. The sheet's good week came from the engine's favorable calls hitting 54 in 100 against a price of 49 inside the playable range, the first week they have beaten the price; across three weeks they stand at 44, 51 and 54 against prices near 50, so one good week is not yet a pattern.

The dropped legs did about as well as the kept ones again: eight of the thirteen players removed for usage hit, including Meyers (JAX) 7 catches, McCaffrey (SF) 75 yards and Darnold (SEA) 379 yards in his first game back. Two weeks of usage were no better a filter than one. From Week 4 the sheet shows the engine's candidates with usage as information, and removes only players who are out or whose quarterback changed.

The model's unders carried information for the second week running: legs it had five or more points under the price hit 46 in 100 against a price of 55.

Role terms are still not built. Week 5 is the first week players have four games of this season, which is when the engine's validated regime begins and last season's roles stop driving the numbers.

The picks

Book says is how often the price says it should hit. Model says is how often we think it hits. When ours is higher, that gap is the whole reason to bet. Odds are DraftKings prices at capture and move.

Every leg carries its reasons as bullets. Singles first, then the same-game pairs that only make sense together.

Longer parlays across bet types (lottery tickets)

Cross-game slips built from the best-value leg in each game across every market, one leg per game, so the price is exactly the product of the legs. A leg qualifies only if it clears the model's 3-point bar in the 35% to 75% book band, is not a mover, carries no new-quarterback or teammate-absence flag, was not rejected in this week's review, and the player's own record last season at that rung is at least what the price asks. Every added leg multiplies both the payout and the chance of losing; these hit a few times a season at best.

How the picks are made

Each game is simulated thousands of times as one offense: the play count, the split between dropbacks and runs, every receiver's targets, catches and yards, every back's carries and yards, and the quarterback's passing line as the sum of what his receivers do plus the throws to everyone else. A quarterback's passing yards and his receiver's yards are therefore priced together, and a back's carries fall in the same simulated games where the passing volume rises.

Behind that sit every receiver's route share, target rate, depth of target, catch rate and yards per catch, both teams' tempo, the total and spread, venue, kickoff window and forecast. The opposing defense enters as five measured terms (yards per target, catch rate, passing touchdowns per attempt, yards per carry and rushing touchdowns per carry allowed, each relative to the league and shrunk hard because defense barely repeats year to year) plus the total and spread. Teammates share the game's pass volume, so paired legs are priced together. A leg makes the list only when the model's number beats the price by a clear margin, the player's own record supports it, and a plain-language reason survives. Games a teammate missed count at 30%, games under a different quarterback at 50%, deep rungs are excluded, and players on a new team are shown but never picked.

The lean
Jared Goff (DET) 250+ passing yards at -169.
  • Detroit throws: 39 and 38 attempts in the first two weeks, 206 yards against New Orleans and 327 with 4 touchdowns at Buffalo. He cleared 250 in 11 of 17 games last season (65%); the price says 62 and the model 67.
  • The Jets' pass defense is a plus for him by last season's numbers, and if it repeats in full the model's number rises to 73, eleven points over the price. Detroit is a 6.5-point favorite in a 47.5-total game at home.
  • A short price for a small gap: this is the surest leg on the board rather than the biggest, and the return reflects that.
  • Opponent, with numbers: NYJ allowed 224.18 passing yards a game last year against a league average of 224.68 (16th fewest of 32), 7.41 yards per attempt (7.02 league, 8th most of 32) while facing 30.2 attempts a game (32.0 league), and a quarterback reached 250 against them in 5 of 17 games (league average 6.1; 9th fewest of 32). NYJ blitzed on 31% of dropbacks (league 30%); blitzing raises sacks and touchdown passes and lowers completions, and the model applies that mix. A plus for this leg.
  • Against defenses like NYJ: the 8 closest to NYJ's pass defense last season, judged on yards per attempt, completion rate, sack rate, touchdowns per attempt, blitz rate. yards per attempt allowed: NYJ 7.36, league 7.04; the group: CHI 7.64, ARI 7.24, DAL 8.15, CIN 7.84, WAS 8.12, SF 7.06, TB 7.63, NE 6.66. Every quarterback against that group last season reached 250 passing yards in 39 games of 100, against 26 versus everyone else and 23 against NYJ itself.
  • By tier: NYJ's pass defense was bottom ten last season on yards per attempt allowed. His record by defense tier, top ten: 2 of 4 in 2025 (225, 168, 255, 256); 2 of 4 in 2024 (292, 85, 240, 303); middle twelve: 3 of 6 in 2025 (202, 203, 284, 279, 338, 197); 4 of 6 in 2024 (307, 280, 145, 283, 494, 231); bottom ten: 6 of 7 in 2025 (334, 258, 241, 320, 309, 364, 331); 4 of 7 in 2024 (217, 199, 315, 412, 269, 221, 336). The lean
Tony Pollard (TEN) 60+ rushing yards at -110.
  • Fourteen carries for 64 last week after 7 in the opener; Tyjae Spears is questionable with an ankle. He cleared 60 in 9 of 17 games last season; the price says 41 and the model 63, 69 if the Giants' run defense repeats last year.
  • Held to Lean: the game total is 38.5, the lowest of the week, and the Week 2 Play on him lost on volume before last week's rebound.
  • Opponent, with numbers: NYG allowed 5.41 yards per carry last year against a league average of 4.38 (1st most of 32), 145 rushing yards a game against 116, and the opposing lead back reached 60 yards in 13 of 17 games (league average 9.5; 2nd most of 32). A plus for this leg.
  • Against defenses like NYG: the 8 closest to NYG's run defense last season, judged on yards per carry, rushing yards per game, rushing touchdowns per carry, how often the lead back reached 60. yards per carry allowed: NYG 5.41, league 4.37; the group: CIN 5.24, CHI 5.06, BUF 5.16, WAS 4.79, MIA 4.83, DAL 4.73, NYJ 4.43, ARI 4.43. He reached 60 rushing yards against that group in 2025: 1 of 1 (67); 2024: 4 of 6 (82, 62, 88, 61, 35, 45). Every back against that group last season reached 60 rushing yards in 30 games of 100, against 22 versus everyone else and 35 against NYG itself.
  • By tier: NYG's run defense was bottom ten last season on yards per carry allowed. His record by defense tier, top ten: 6 of 12 in 2025 (60, 45, 64, 34, 44, 22, 20, 60, 161, 102, 85, 48); 2 of 5 in 2024 (62, 14, 93, 15, 35); middle twelve: 2 of 4 in 2025 (92, 18, 56, 104); 7 of 8 in 2024 (88, 61, 94, 128, 119, 102, 45, 62); bottom ten: 1 of 1 in 2025 (67); 1 of 3 in 2024 (82, 44, 35). Every back last season reached 60 rushing yards against top-ten defenses 20 times in 100, middle twelve 23, bottom ten 30.
  • Worst case: Model 63 in 100 as built. If NYG's defense repeats last season in full, 68. The price says 52. Holds in the worst case.

George Kittle (SF) 5+ receptions at +123.

ARI blitzed on 31% of dropbacks (league 30%); blitzing raises sacks and touchdown passes and lowers completions, and the model applies that mix. A plus for this leg.

  • By tier: ARI's pass defense was middle twelve last season on yards per attempt allowed. His record by defense tier, top ten: 1 of 4 in 2025 (4, 4, 4, 5); 2 of 3 in 2024 (4, 5, 8); middle twelve: 3 of 5 in 2025 (0, 4, 9, 6, 7); 4 of 7 in 2024 (7, 4, 6, 3, 6, 1, 8); bottom ten: 2 of 2 in 2025 (6, 8); 3 of 5 in 2024 (8, 6, 6, 4, 2).
